societies.name: Passengers — Avalon’s prematurely awakened residents
societies.society: Jim and Aurora’s continuing shipboard household

scope.period: The prematurely awakened pair’s continuing residence, including life after the reactor repair
scope.population: Jim and Aurora while alive and awake aboard Avalon
exclusions: Hibernating colonists and crew as leisure citizens
Gus as a durable third resident
Different events in early screenplay drafts

societies.description:
Jim and Aurora become long-term residents of a largely automatic passenger environment, with living space, meals, entertainment and medical machinery already operating around them. Their continuing support is not paid out of current wages. This makes the pair a narrow post-work household comparison rather than a claim about all future humanity. Passenger class affects food privileges, and serious malfunctions threaten even basic survival, so the guarantee estimate is moderately strong rather than unlimited or secure under every condition.

The ship’s services enforce a designed hierarchy of passenger and employee permissions. That supports a concentrated institutional-control estimate near zero; a talking interface and automatic flight do not establish an independent AI sovereign. Gus’s employee access helps the pair reach systems that their passenger status cannot command. Human work also remains indispensable when the reactor fails, and Aurora continues writing. Their later home does not supply an exact lifetime participation rate. Sleeping travelers and people not yet born are excluded from the denominator, while the eventual successful voyage is not proof of a post-work colony at its destination.

guarantees.basis: Long-term automatic passenger services support the awake pair without current wages, but class restrictions, failed hibernation and infrastructure breakdown qualify security.

control.basis: Access follows concentrated passenger/employee permissions; the ship interface is not shown to own the infrastructure or set an autonomous political constitution.

nonworking.basis: Writing, maintenance and emergency repair remain useful work; neither continuous leisure nor a stable work census follows from the long time aboard.

evidence.claim: The pair remain awake with ship services, repair the failing reactor and subsequently live out their lives aboard.

uncertainties: An accidental but continuing two-human supported household, not a temporary holiday or proof of universal welfare.
Infrastructure repair is actual human work, not dispensable make-work.
The guarantee interval reflects both provision and severe technical failure.
Neither sleeping population ratios nor unknown later descendants create a participation estimate.

review.method: Second pass against the gathered passages, including explicit uncertainty; no independent reviewer

decisions.reason: The Collective’s social control is not a verified automatic material-support economy.
decisions.analysis: The short reference check does not establish labor replacement or work-independent household distribution.

decisions.reason: Avalon actually supports a continuing awake household without current wages, with class restrictions and real human repair work disclosed.
Pandorum’s failed transport and predatory survivors do not form a verified functioning post-work order.
decisions.analysis: Stasis, technical capability and an eventual escape do not establish a durable distribution constitution for awake people.
decisions.follow_up: Do not count hibernation as leisure or invent the post-escape colony’s economy.

decisions.reason: UTS privilege and excluded salvage workers do not establish the elite’s labor-independent provisioning mechanism.
decisions.analysis: The official synopsis establishes inequality and useful paid work, not automatic necessities or productive ownership beyond corporate setting.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper lore; do not convert noncitizenship into nonemployment.

decisions.reason: Jung_E depicts real industrial and human-derived military work rather than a demonstrated general post-work support order.
decisions.analysis: A contract buying brain data and paying one family’s expenses does not establish population-wide work independence.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a cognitive-labor and personhood comparison.

decisions.reason: Vesper’s seed monopoly still depends on real subsistence and biological production work.
decisions.analysis: Artificial scarcity and wealth are not sufficient for a zero variant without available replacement of the relevant productive labor.
decisions.follow_up: Keep as a biotechnology monopoly comparison; do not infer an unseen citadel welfare constitution.

decisions.reason: Noctis’s mixed human-robot society does not have a verified work-independent access system in the quick reference.
decisions.analysis: Brain farms and detective work establish actual activity and exploitation, not a general provisioning mechanism.

decisions.reason: The departing robots do not yet have a verified settled material-access constitution.
decisions.analysis: Carlos’s human-derived identity prevents treating all participants as mere hardware, but departure and autonomy still do not establish support rights or the active community’s economic rules.
decisions.follow_up: Do not manufacture a new regime from the destination left unspecified.

decisions.reason: Draag technology and Om subordination do not establish an automatic provision system for a scoped population.
decisions.analysis: Meditation is not a nonworking census, and kept humans and wild Oms cannot be assigned identical access rights.
decisions.follow_up: Skip deeper film or source-novel reading.

decisions.reason: Gandahar’s plentiful food and engineered organisms do not resolve productive labor or distribution.
decisions.analysis: The ecological utopia has excluded experimental populations, and abundance does not itself show that work has ceased to allocate necessities.
decisions.follow_up: Skip a full viewing or novel reconstruction; do not mistake biological technology for literal absence of technology.

decisions.reason: Metamorphis uses captive people as biological resources rather than supporting a human post-work community.
decisions.analysis: Machine servants do not make their controller an AI or their human victims leisured beneficiaries.

decisions.reason: Alpha 60’s control over thought and behavior does not establish Alphaville’s automatic material economy.
decisions.analysis: An AI ruler can coexist with many different labor and distribution systems; the checked account does not settle which one applies.

review_notes: Twelve short-check dispositions and one continuing-household admission.
Avalon’s long-lived awake residents are scoped separately from hibernating travelers; human repairs, writing and passenger-class restrictions stay visible.
Unrelated Equals, UTS and Gandahar search hits were discarded. Biological technology is eligible in principle but still needs an actual economic mechanism.
A human-derived android is recognized as such; that does not supply missing allocation rules for a departing robot population.
